issues.display_title: Issue #552: App-to-App Data Exchange Downtime Resilience
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: App-to-App Data Exchange Downtime Resilience

  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Task Specification: docs/tasks/2026-10-16/app_to_app_data_exchange_resilience.md

1. Summary

Implemented fail-fast safety and M2M service account token resilience in panorra-api-go-new:

  1. Redis M2M Token Caching (src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak.go):

    • Implemented hierarchical caching: In-Memory Cache → Redis (keycloak:m2m_token:{client_id}) → Keycloak Token Endpoint.
    • Strict TTL: expires_in - 60s.
    • Concurrency protection: sync.Mutex (fetchingMu) prevents multiple goroutines from fetching concurrently on cache expiration.
    • Offline handling: If Keycloak is down or times out, immediately returns an error.

  2. Abort Outbound Requests on Keycloak Failure (src/Utils/GoThru/GoThru.go):

    • In FetchVirtualTours, if Keycloak.GetServiceToken() returns an error, the outbound request to the GoThru API is aborted immediately before invoking httpClient.Do(req).
    • 0 network requests are made to GoThru API during Keycloak downtime.
    • In src/Action/V1/Posts/TourVerification.go, trail post tour verification returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway without hanging.

  3. Keycloak Outage Interception in Auth & Registration:

    • In src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakHandlers.go and src/Action/V1/Register/ValidateRegister.go:
    • Differentiates authentic token invalidity (HTTP 401) from service unreachability / timeouts (HTTP 502 Bad Gateway with "Authentication service is temporarily unavailable").

2. Files Created & Updated

Created

  • src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak_test.go: Unit tests verifying Redis M2M caching, cache hit on Keycloak offline, and error propagation.
  • docs/tasks/2026-10-16/app_to_app_data_exchange_resilience.md: Specification document.
  • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-16/app_to_app_data_exchange_resilience_impl.md: This implementation document.

Updated

  • src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak.go: Added Redis caching with key keycloak:m2m_token:{client_id} and TTL expires_in - 60s. Added ResetTokenCache() and SetRedisHooks.
  • src/Utils/GoThru/GoThru.go: Aborts request to GoThru API when Keycloak service token acquisition fails.
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakHandlers.go: Returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway when Keycloak userinfo service is unreachable.
  • src/Action/V1/Register/ValidateRegister.go: Intercepts Keycloak service outage and returns HTTP 502.

3. Example Responses & Outage Contracts

Example 1: Keycloak SSO Login During Outage

When Keycloak is down, requests to /auth/keycloak abort immediately and return HTTP 502 Bad Gateway:

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/keycloak" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "some-keycloak-access-token"
  }'

Response (HTTP 502 Bad Gateway):

{
  "statusCode": 502,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Gateway",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Authentication service is temporarily unavailable"
    }
  }
}

Example 2: Keycloak Registration Validation During Outage

When Keycloak is unreachable, registration pre-validation (POST /register/validate?type=keycloak) returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway:

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/register/validate?type=keycloak" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "some-keycloak-access-token"
  }'

Response (HTTP 502 Bad Gateway):

{
  "statusCode": 502,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Gateway",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Authentication service is temporarily unavailable"
    }
  }
}

Example 3: Trail Post Verification When Keycloak Is Offline

When publishing a trail post, tour ownership verification aborts without calling GoThru API and fails fast:

Response (HTTP 502 Bad Gateway):

{
  "statusCode": 502,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Gateway",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Failed to contact GoThru provider",
      "input": "trail.points[0].url"
    }
  }
}

4. Verification

# Run unit tests
go test -count=1 -v ./src/Utils/Keycloak/... ./src/Action/V1/Auth/... ./src/Action/V1/Register/...

# Verify compilation
go build ./...

Results:

  • src/Utils/Keycloak: PASS (4 tests, 0 failures)
  • src/Action/V1/Auth: PASS (27 tests, 0 failures)
  • src/Action/V1/Register: PASS (11 tests, 0 failures)
  • Compilation: Clean build with 0 errors / 0 warnings.
  • Area: Auth / Keycloak SSO / Inter-Service Communication
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new (Mutation & Auth Service)
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Related Ecosystem Issues:
    • Issue #21: Task: App-to-App Data Exchange Downtime Resilience (Reference specification: docs/app-to-app-data-exchange-resilience-task-template.md)
    • Issue #9: Epic: GoThru App-to-App Data Exchange Integration
    • Issue #11: Task 2: Implement Requestor Capabilities (Fetching from others)
    • Issue #20: Client Resilience, Pre-flight Health Probe & Emergency Fallback Login
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak.go
    • src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak_test.go
    • src/Utils/GoThru/GoThru.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/TourVerification.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakHandlers.go
    • src/Action/V1/Register/ValidateRegister.go
  • Date: 2026-10-16

1. Problem

In panorra-api-go-new, backend operations occasionally query the GoThru Provider API on behalf of users—specifically during trail post tour verification (TourVerification.go). Under normal conditions, this relies on Keycloak's OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant (M2M service account token).

Previously:

  1. In-Memory Only Caching: Keycloak service tokens were cached solely in an in-memory struct without persistence across pod/process restarts.
  2. Missing Redis Cache Key Convention: Tokens were not cached in Redis under the standard ecosystem key keycloak:m2m_token:{client_id} with strict TTL expires_in - 60s.
  3. No Fail-Fast Safety on Keycloak Outages: If Keycloak experienced downtime, timeouts, or network partitions:
    • Token acquisition would fail, potentially hanging connection pools.
    • S2S calls would attempt unauthenticated or hanging requests to GoThru API.
    • User SSO login (/auth/keycloak) and registration validation (/register/validate) would return misleading 401s or generic unhandled errors instead of explicitly signaling an authentication service outage (HTTP 502 Bad Gateway).

2. Scope

  1. Redis M2M Token Cache (src/Utils/Keycloak/Keycloak.go):

    • Implement hierarchical cache: In-Memory → Redis (keycloak:m2m_token:{client_id}) → Keycloak Token Endpoint.
    • Set strict Redis TTL to expires_in - 60 seconds.
    • Prevent thundering-herd concurrent fetches using double-check locking with sync.Mutex.
    • If Keycloak is unreachable or times out: return ("", err) immediately without hanging.

  2. Abort GoThru API Requests on Keycloak Failure (src/Utils/GoThru/GoThru.go):

    • In FetchVirtualTours, check if Keycloak.GetServiceToken() succeeds.
    • If Keycloak fails (timeout, connection refused, error):
      • Abort outbound request immediately before calling httpClient.Do(req).
      • Zero network calls sent to GoThru API.
      • Return error: fmt.Errorf("keycloak: failed to obtain service token: %w", err).
    • In src/Action/V1/Posts/TourVerification.go, verify trail tours fails fast and returns HTTP 502 without hanging.

  3. Keycloak Outage Interception in Auth & Registration:

    • In src/Action/V1/Auth/KeycloakHandlers.go (LoginKeycloak / authenticateKeycloak):
      • If token is rejected by Keycloak: return HTTP 401 Unauthorized ("Unauthorized GoThru token").
      • If Keycloak server is offline, times out, or returns 5xx: return HTTP 502 Bad Gateway ("Authentication service is temporarily unavailable").
    • In src/Action/V1/Register/ValidateRegister.go:
      • Distinguish genuine token invalidity (401) from Keycloak downtime/timeout (502).

3. Behavior Boundary

  • No New Environment Variables Required: Reuses existing KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET, and GOTHRU_API_BASE_URL.
  • Database Safety: READ-ONLY by default. Zero database schema modifications or migrations.
  • Fail-Fast Safety: Guarantees threads do not hang during Keycloak network drops.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • When Keycloak is running: M2M token is fetched and cached in Redis with key keycloak:m2m_token:{client_id} and TTL expires_in - 60s.
  • When Keycloak is offline but token is in Redis: token is served from cache with zero network calls to Keycloak.
  • When Keycloak is offline/timeout and token is not cached:
    • Requests towards GoThru API are aborted immediately (0 calls made).
    • Keycloak SSO login and registration validation return HTTP 502 Bad Gateway with message "Authentication service is temporarily unavailable".
  • All unit tests pass with zero failures.

issues.display_title: Issue #553: Request Emergency Email Magic Link API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Request Emergency Email Magic Link API

  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Task Specification: docs/tasks/2026-10-16/request_magic_link_api.md
  • Related Ecosystem Issue: #22: Emergency Email Magic Link Login Fallback

1. Summary

Implemented the POST /auth/magic-link/request endpoint allowing users to initiate an emergency passwordless sign-in flow during Keycloak downtime:

  1. Email Parsing & Validation:

    • Validates email syntax using net/mail.ParseAddress. Returns 422 if invalid.
    • Checks users table for matching account.
    • Unregistered Account Handling: If the email does not exist in the database, returns BuildUnregisteredResponse (HTTP 400 Bad Request with "message": "Please Register First", "code": "unregistered") to instruct the user to register first.

  2. Rate Limiting & Security Hardening:

    • Enforces max 3 requests per 15 minutes per email using Redis key magic_link:rate:{email}. Returns HTTP 429 when threshold is reached.
    • Generates a cryptographically random 32-byte hex nonce via crypto/rand.
    • Stores nonce in Redis mapped to email: magic_link:nonce:{nonce} -> {email} with 15-minute TTL.
    • Strict Privacy Rule: user_id is never included in the token payload or Redis mapping. Token payload contains only sub (email), nonce, type ("magic_link"), iat, and exp.

  3. Transactional Email Dispatch:

    • Builds verification URL: https://<PWA>/auth/magic-link/verify?token=<token>.
    • Queues message into RabbitMQ (${RABBITMQ_PREFIX}_send_email) with template "email_magic_link".
    • Renders src/Utils/EmailTemplate/templates/email_magic_link.html using the GoThru design concept with image https://panorra.com/assets/email-template/image/keycloak-downtime.png.

2. Files Created & Updated

Created

  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go: Implemented RequestMagicLink handler.
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink_test.go: Unit tests for email validation, anti-enumeration, rate limiting, and nonce generation.
  • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/templates/email_magic_link.html: GoThru-branded responsive email template.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Request Magic Link.yml: API collection documentation.
  • docs/tasks/2026-10-16/request_magic_link_api.md: Task specification.
  • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-16/request_magic_link_api_impl.md: This implementation document.

Updated

  • src/Controllers/V1/AuthController.go: Added RequestMagicLink controller method.
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go: Registered POST /auth/magic-link/request.
  • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/EmailTemplate.go: Registered "email_magic_link" in template registry.

3. Example Usage & API Contracts

Endpoint

POST /auth/magic-link/request

Headers

Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

Request & Response Examples

Example 1: Successful Request (Valid User)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }'

Response (HTTP 200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "message": "If this email is registered, a magic login link has been sent."
  }
}

Example 2: Unregistered Email (Prompt to Register First)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "unregistered.user@example.com"
  }'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "message": "Please Register First",
    "valid": true,
    "code": "unregistered"
  }
}

Example 3: Missing Email Field

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Email is required",
      "input": "email"
    }
  }
}

Example 4: Invalid Email Syntax

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "not-a-valid-email-format"
  }'

Response (HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity):

{
  "statusCode": 422,
  "data": {
    "status": "Unprocessable Entity",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Invalid email address format",
      "input": "email"
    }
  }
}

Example 5: Rate Limit Exceeded (> 3 requests in 15 minutes)

curl -X POST "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/request" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com"
  }'

Response (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests):

{
  "statusCode": 429,
  "data": {
    "status": "Too Many Requests",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Too many magic link requests. Please wait a few minutes before trying again."
    }
  }
}

4. Verification

# Run unit tests
go test -count=1 -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth/... ./src/Utils/EmailTemplate/...

# Verify compilation
go build ./...

Results:

  • All tests passed cleanly (0 failures).
  • Build compiled with 0 errors.
  • Area: Auth / Emergency Fallback / Passwordless Authentication
  • Endpoint: POST /auth/magic-link/request
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Related Ecosystem Issues:
    • Issue #22: Emergency Email Magic Link Login Fallback
    • Issue #20: Client Resilience & Pre-flight Health Probe
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink_test.go
    • src/Controllers/V1/AuthController.go
    • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go
    • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/templates/email_magic_link.html
    • src/Utils/EmailTemplate/EmailTemplate.go
    • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Request Magic Link.yml
  • Date: 2026-10-16

1. Problem & Context

During extended Keycloak outages or maintenance windows, users cannot log in through SSO. Local passwords cannot be used because password desynchronization risks locking users out of their accounts.

An emergency passwordless login mechanism is required via Email Magic Link:

  • Users provide only their registered email address.
  • The system validates the email, generates a single-use token, and dispatches a secure sign-in link to their inbox.
  • Security Rule (No user_id Exposure): To eliminate the risk of exposing internal database keys or allowing attackers to enumerate account IDs, user_id must NOT be included in the token payload, the Redis cache mapping, or the verification URL.

2. Scope

  1. Request Endpoint (POST /auth/magic-link/request):

    • Accept JSON payload: { "email": "user@example.com" }.
    • Validate RFC 5322 email address format.
    • Query local users table: 
      SELECT u.id, u.encrypt, u.fullname, u.email, u.username, u.password, u.is_active, u.is_back, u.is_email_verified, ud.onboarding_completed, urd.id AS users_request_delete_id
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN users_request_delete urd ON u.id = urd.user_id
LEFT JOIN user_detail ud ON u.id = ud.user_id
WHERE LOWER(u.email) = ? LIMIT 1
    • Anti-Enumeration Protection: If email is unregistered, blacklisted, or inactive, return a generic HTTP 200 response ("If this email is registered, a magic login link has been sent.") without revealing whether the account exists.

  2. Rate Limiting:

    • Redis-based sliding counter: maximum 3 requests per 15 minutes per email.
    • Returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests if the limit is exceeded.

  3. Cryptographic Nonce & JWT Generation (Strictly Without user_id):

    • Generate a 32-byte cryptographic random nonce (crypto/rand).
    • Store nonce in Redis mapped to email: 
      SET magic_link:nonce:{nonce} "{user_email}" EX 900
    • Sign a JWT token using JWT_SECRET with 15-minute expiration: 
      {
  "sub": "user@example.com",
  "nonce": "c4b8e2f9...",
  "type": "magic_link",
  "iat": 1729000000,
  "exp": 1729000900
}
    • Build verification URL: https://<app_domain>/auth/magic-link/verify?token=... (strictly without user_id).

  4. Transactional Email Delivery:

    • Enqueue email to RabbitMQ queue _send_email.
    • Uses template src/Utils/EmailTemplate/templates/email_magic_link.html.
    • Features GoThru brand typography, illustration https://panorra.com/assets/email-template/image/keycloak-downtime.png, action button [ Sign in to GoThru ], 15-minute expiry warning, and security footer.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • No user_id in Token: Eliminates exposure of internal database identifiers.
  • Timing & Enumeration Resistant: Identical HTTP 200 response returned whether an email exists or not.
  • No New Environment Variables: Reuses existing JWT_SECRET, RABBITMQ_PREFIX, REDIS_*, and WEB_URL.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /auth/magic-link/request validates email format (422 on invalid format, 400 on empty).
  • Returns generic 200 for non-existent or inactive emails.
  • Stores nonce mapped to email in Redis with 15-minute TTL.
  • Publishes email payload to RabbitMQ queue for registered users.
  • Rejects requests exceeding 3 attempts in 15 minutes with HTTP 429.
  • API Collection documentation created with request and response examples.

issues.display_title: Issue #554: Verify Emergency Email Magic Link API
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Verify Emergency Email Magic Link API

  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Task Specification: docs/tasks/2026-10-16/verify_magic_link_api.md
  • Related Ecosystem Issue: #22: Emergency Email Magic Link Login Fallback

1. Summary

Implemented the GET /auth/magic-link/verify endpoint handling email magic link verification and authentication session issuance:

  1. Pure GET Request Handling:

    • Reads token directly from URL query parameter ?token=....
    • Requires no request body/payload, ensuring complete compatibility with direct browser clicks from email inboxes.

  2. Cryptographic Validation & Nonce Invalidation:

    • Parses the JWT and validates its HMAC-SHA256 signature using JWT_SECRET.
    • Validates that type == "magic_link" and that the token has not expired.
    • Single-Use Enforcement: Atomically retrieves and deletes the nonce key (magic_link:nonce:{nonce}) from Redis.
    • If the nonce was already deleted (or expired), immediately returns HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Magic link has already been used or has expired"), preventing replay attacks.
    • Validates that the email associated with the nonce matches the JWT sub claim.

  3. User Resolution & Session Generation:

    • Resolves user profile from database using verified email without exposing or requiring user_id in the token.
    • Automatically marks unverified emails as verified (is_email_verified = true).
    • Reactivates accounts if deletion was pending.
    • Refreshes session cache in Redis via RefreshUserSession.
    • Generates Panorra Hasura JWT via RegisterFunctions.GenerateUserJWT.
    • Returns standard login response envelope with "fallback": "magic_link".

2. Files Created & Updated

Created

  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go: Implemented VerifyMagicLink handler.
  • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink_test.go: Unit tests for missing token, invalid signature, expired token, and nonce replay prevention.
  • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml: API collection documentation for GET verification.
  • docs/tasks/2026-10-16/verify_magic_link_api.md: Task specification.
  • docs/tasks/implementations/2026-10-16/verify_magic_link_api_impl.md: This implementation document.

Updated

  • src/Controllers/V1/AuthController.go: Added VerifyMagicLink controller method.
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go: Registered GET /auth/magic-link/verify.
  • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes_test.go: Added route registration tests.

3. Example Usage & API Contracts

Endpoint

GET /auth/magic-link/verify

Query Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description
token string Yes Signed magic link JWT token received via email
ec string No Optional response encryption flag ("true" / "false")

Request & Response Examples

Example 1: Successful Verification (Valid Magic Link Click)

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response (HTTP 200 OK):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Login success",
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJodHRwczovL2hhc3VyYS5pby9qd3QvY2xhaW1zIjp7...}",
    "total": 0,
    "fallback": "magic_link",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "username": "user_example",
    "is_back": false,
    "onboarding_completed": true,
    "is_complete": {
      "is_password": true,
      "is_email": true,
      "is_email_verified": true
    }
  }
}

Example 2: Missing Token Parameter

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Token is required",
      "input": "token"
    }
  }
}

Example 3: Link Already Used (Replay Attack)

(Triggered when a user clicks the same link a second time)

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify?token=already-consumed-token..." \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Magic link has already been used or has expired"
    }
  }
}

Example 4: Expired Link (> 15 minutes elapsed)

curl -X GET "https://api.panorra.com/auth/magic-link/verify?token=expired-jwt-token..." \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response (HTTP 400 Bad Request):

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "Bad Request",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "message": "Magic link is invalid or has expired"
    }
  }
}

4. Verification

# Run unit tests
go test -count=1 -v ./src/Action/V1/Auth/... ./src/Routes/V1/...

# Verify compilation
go build ./...

Results:

  • All tests passed cleanly (0 failures).
  • Build compiled with 0 errors.
  • Area: Auth / Emergency Fallback / Passwordless Authentication
  • Endpoint: GET /auth/magic-link/verify
  • Target Project: panorra-api-go-new
  • Related Project Board: Panorra API Go Get - Development (View 2: Development - Board)
  • Related Ecosystem Issues:
    • Issue #22: Emergency Email Magic Link Login Fallback
    • Issue #20: Client Resilience & Pre-flight Health Probe
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink.go
    • src/Action/V1/Auth/MagicLink_test.go
    • src/Controllers/V1/AuthController.go
    • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes.go
    • src/Routes/V1/AuthRoutes_test.go
    • api-collection/Panorra API Post/Auth/Verify Magic Link.yml
  • Date: 2026-10-16

1. Problem & Context

Once a user receives the emergency login email containing their magic link, they click the button or copy-paste the URL into their browser.

Requirements:

  • Pure GET Request: Because this action is triggered directly when a user clicks the link in an email client (or when the frontend redirects), the endpoint must be GET /auth/magic-link/verify with the token passed via query parameter ?token=... without requiring a POST body/payload.
  • Single-Use Nonce Enforcement (Replay Attack Prevention): The link must work only once. The moment it is validated, the security nonce stored in Redis must be burned (DEL). Any subsequent attempts to use the same link must be rejected.
  • Zero user_id Exposure: Identity is verified strictly through verified email ownership extracted from the cryptographically signed JWT sub claim.
  • Session Issuance: The endpoint must issue a standard authenticated session (Hasura JWT) and return the standard Panorra login response envelope with "fallback": "magic_link".

2. Scope

  1. Verify Endpoint (GET /auth/magic-link/verify):

    • Read token from URL query string: c.Query("token").
    • If token is missing, return HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Token is required").

  2. Cryptographic Validation & Nonce Burning:

    • Parse and verify HMAC signature and expiration (exp) with JWT_SECRET.
    • Validate claim type == "magic_link".
    • Extract nonce and sub (email).
    • Atomically check and delete nonce from Redis: 
      GET magic_link:nonce:{nonce}
DEL magic_link:nonce:{nonce}
    • If nonce does not exist or has already been deleted, immediately reject with HTTP 400 Bad Request ("Magic link has already been used or has expired").
    • Verify that the email stored in the nonce matches sub.

  3. User Resolution & Session Generation:

    • Query local users table by verified email: 
      SELECT u.id, u.encrypt, u.fullname, u.email, u.username, u.password, u.is_active, u.is_back, u.is_email_verified, ud.onboarding_completed, urd.id AS users_request_delete_id
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN users_request_delete urd ON u.id = urd.user_id
LEFT JOIN user_detail ud ON u.id = ud.user_id
WHERE LOWER(u.email) = ? LIMIT 1
    • If user not found, return HTTP 404 Not Found.
    • If user was unverified, automatically mark is_email_verified = true (clicking the link proves email ownership).
    • Reactivate user if pending deletion (ReactivateUserIfRequested).
    • Refresh user session and cache in Redis (RefreshUserSession).
    • Generate standard Panorra Hasura JWT (RegisterFunctions.GenerateUserJWT).
    • Build login response envelope with "fallback": "magic_link".

3. Behavior Boundary

  • GET Only: Accepts query parameter ?token=... without payload.
  • Single-Use Guarantee: Replay attacks are impossible because the nonce is destroyed on first verification.
  • No user_id in Token: User identity resolved from email claim only.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /auth/magic-link/verify?token=... accepts query parameter and returns HTTP 400 if token is missing.
  • Rejects expired tokens (> 15 minutes) with HTTP 400.
  • Burns nonce on first use; second use returns HTTP 400.
  • Returns standard login response with valid JWT token for legitimate users.
  • API Collection documentation created with GET method and response examples.
